title: What Happens If You Cry In Space?
sources: NASA Flight Experience: Tear Behavior in Microgravity (Chris Hadfield Experiment)
European Space Agency (ESA): Fluid Dynamics in Zero Gravity

lines.text: What actually happens if an astronaut cries in space?
On Earth, gravity pulls tears down your cheeks, but in zero gravity,
tears don't fall at all! Instead, surface tension binds the liquid,
forming a giant, growing water bubble directly over your eyeballs!
Astronaut Chris Hadfield said it stings violently and blinds you until you grab a towel to wipe it off!
lines.caps: IT *STINGS & BLINDS YOU | UNTIL YOU *WIPE IT!
